taskDescriptions.do: Choose the main activity that the child wearing the camera is DOING.
taskDescriptions.see: Choose the main activity that the child wearing the camera is SEEING (usually something other people are doing in front of the child).

do.being moved around: The child with the camera on is being carried, pushed in a stroller or cart, or otherwise moved by someone else. Choose this over "looking around" when the child is being moved.
do.crawling: Moving on hands and knees (or scooting) along the floor. The camera view is usually low, close to the floor, and moving.
do.walking: Moving on foot (walking, toddling, running, cruising along furniture) when moving is the main thing happening. If something more salient is going on, such as playing, code that instead.
do.looking around: The child's gaze moves around the environment and nothing more salient is happening. Children are almost always looking around, so use this only when no other activity applies.
do.cleaning: Tidying, wiping, sweeping, mopping, washing dishes, doing laundry, or putting things away.
do.cooking: Preparing food: chopping, stirring, using the stove or oven, or assembling a meal. Eating the food is "eating/drinking".
do.eating/drinking: Eating or drinking, including being fed, drinking from a cup or bottle, and meal or snack time at a table or high chair.
do.getting dressed: Putting on or taking off clothes, shoes, hats, jackets, or diapers.
do.reading time: Looking at a book and reading it, sometimes indicated by pointing at and naming pictures in a book or the presence of another person. This usually involves another person. Handling a book without reading it counts as playing with household object.
do.playing with nature: Playing with or exploring natural things such as sand, dirt, water, leaves, sticks, plants, rocks, or snow. Usually includes children playing with plants.
do.playing without toy: Playing that does not involve an object, such as peekaboo, tickling, chasing, rough-and-tumble, or clapping games.
do.playing with pet: Petting, feeding, or playing with pets like dogs and cats.
do.playing with toy: Playing with an object made to be a toy, such as blocks, dolls, balls, stuffed animals, toy vehicles, or puzzles.
do.playing with household object: Playing with an everyday object that is not a toy, such as books, containers, utensils, boxes, remote controls, or keys.
do.playing with instrument: Making sound or music with a musical instrument such as a piano, drum, or guitar.
do.drawing: Drawing, coloring, painting, or writing with markers, crayons, chalk, pencils, pens, or paint.
do.screen time: Watching or using a screen such as a TV, phone, tablet, or computer.
do.other: A clear activity that fits none of the categories above. Describe it in the text box that appears.
do.no activity: No activity can be identified, for example because the view is blocked or the footage is too dark or blurry to tell.

see.crawling: Someone in view, such as a sibling or another baby, is crawling or scooting along the floor, and that is the main thing happening.
see.walking: People in view are walking, toddling or running, and that movement is the main thing happening (for example, a caregiver walking ahead, or people passing by on a sidewalk). If they are doing something more salient, such as playing, code that instead.
see.cleaning: Someone in view, or the child's own hands, is tidying, wiping, sweeping, mopping, washing dishes, doing laundry, or putting things away.
see.cooking: Someone in view is preparing food: chopping, stirring, using the stove or oven, or assembling a meal. Seeing people eat the food is "eating/drinking".
see.conversing: The child is attending to people talking (for example, an adult facing the child and talking to them, or adults talking to each other), with no more salient activity in view.
see.getting dressed: Someone in view is putting on or taking off clothes, shoes, hats, jackets, or diapers. This includes the child being dressed or changed, when the hands doing it are in view.
see.eating/drinking: Someone in view is eating or drinking, or the child is being fed (for example, a spoon or bottle coming toward the camera), or a meal or snack is laid out at the table or high chair.
see.playing with nature: Someone in view, or the child's own hands, is playing with or exploring natural things such as sand, dirt, water, leaves, sticks, plants, rocks, or snow. This includes gardening.
see.playing without toy: Someone in view is playing a game that does not involve an object, such as peekaboo, tickling, chasing, rough-and-tumble, or clapping games.
see.playing with pet: Someone in view is petting, feeding, or playing with a pet like a dog or cat, or a pet is the main thing the child is watching.
see.playing with toy: Someone in view, or the child's own hands, is playing with an object made to be a toy, such as blocks, dolls, balls, stuffed animals, toy vehicles, or puzzles.
see.playing with household object: Someone in view, or the child's own hands, is playing with an everyday object that is not a toy, such as containers, utensils, boxes, remote controls, or keys.
see.playing with instrument: Someone in view is making sound or music with a musical instrument such as a piano, drum, or guitar.
see.dancing: Someone in view is moving rhythmically to music.
see.drawing: Someone in view, or the child's own hands, is drawing, coloring, painting, or writing with markers, crayons, chalk, pencils, pens, or paint.
see.reading time: A book is being read in view: someone is holding a book open toward the child, turning pages, or pointing at and naming pictures. Someone handling a book without reading it counts as playing with household object.
see.screen time: A screen such as a TV, phone, tablet, or computer is showing something, and the child is watching it.
see.other: A clear activity is happening in view that fits none of the categories above. Describe it in the text box that appears.
see.no activity: Nothing identifiable is happening in view (an empty room, scenery passing by, etc.), or the footage is too dark or blurry to tell.

anyoneInteracting: Answer "yes" if another person actively engages with the child during the clip: talking to them, touching, holding, or moving them, pointing things out, handing them objects, making eye contact, or responding to the child. Someone merely being present does not count.
